lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 47, which adds an Include subfolders toggle to the search bar, saved for each folder.
It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
Press Ctrl+F, and a toggle appears beside the search field.
lines.say: Press control F, and a toggle appears beside the search field.

lines.caption: It shows the folder's saved choice, or what Preferences means for this folder.
A click saves the choice in the folder's metadata.
Then the search restarts with the same query.
The search asks one new helper: the saved choice first, else the preference.
The search job then walks the subfolders or stays in the folder, in every view.
Until now, one setting decided subfolder search for every folder. Now each folder can have its own.
Every search goes through one function, so changing it there covers both the list and the tree views.
The location entry shows the toggle only while its text is a search query.
With no saved choice, Local Files Only shows pressed on a local disk and released on a network share.
The click is saved the same way Thunar saves a folder's sort order and zoom.
A new restart-search call hands the same query to the existing search path, so results change at once.
A new helper picks the saved choice or the preference, and a second one turns that into yes or no for this folder.
The search job now asks that helper instead of reading the preference; the rest is unchanged.
A saved choice wins over Preferences, on or off.
With no saved choice, or after clearing it, Preferences decides as before.
Clear Saved Folder View Settings removes the choice, and now shows whenever the folder has saved settings.
To undo it for one folder, clear its settings. Reverting the PR leaves only a harmless unused key.
Six Thunar source files and one extension header change, plus the test script, this page and its narration.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It follows how folder sort and zoom are saved, reuses the search job, and is checked against the issue.
After the review fixes, the Debian package built in this session with no new compiler warnings.
Turning the toggle off left only the top folder's match, and another folder kept the default.
The choice came back on return to the folder, and Clear removed it; each result was asserted.
A search typed by hand into the location bar also re-ran when the toggle was clicked.
The sandbox has no gvfs, so saving to disk and surviving a restart were not tested here.
After the fixes, each screenshot was read and matched to its description.
The script copies each search's results into a scratch folder and checks exactly which files arrive.
A fresh review agent read only the diff and the issue, and found one high and two medium problems; the high and one medium are fixed.
Fixed: the test now checks the actual results, not only metadata that CI cannot write.
Fixed: in split view a stale flag could swallow the re-run; a new restart call clears it.
Writing the choice in the background was tried, then reverted: it caused a warning and a folder reload on every click.
Kept: the fixed click position, and two Clear cases that cannot happen.
CI's own reviews found two high problems and two medium ones, plus lows.
Fixed: the new key was not on the list of metadata Thunar loads, so a saved choice would not survive a restart.
Fixed: closing a window could touch the toggle after it was destroyed.
Fixed: the toggle and the search job now share one rule.
Fixed: a search typed by hand into the location bar now re-runs when you click the toggle.
Accepted: CI can't test a restart without gvfs; adding it is tracked in issue 48.
The remaining lows are kept on purpose, sit in older code, or were refuted.
After the merge, check that the choice survives a restart, how the toggle looks, and the split-view check.
Part 3. Nothing depends on this issue, so only your own check remains.
Flip the toggle, restart Thunar, search again, and run the split-view crash check.
In short: one click now decides, per folder, whether a search looks inside subfolders.
